newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: War crimes experts open mass grave in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: War crimes experts open mass grave in Bosnia.

text.p: Forensic experts have begun exhuming remains from a suspected mass grave in Bosnia, the U.N. war crimes tribunal for former Yugoslavia said on Tuesday.
It said a team of 25 specialists from the prosecutor's office had begun removing human remains from a site in the northern town of Brcko in Serb-controlled territory.

"This grave is related to the indictment issued... in connection with the confinement and the systematic killings of hundreds of Moslem and Croat men from Brcko at the Luka Camp," the tribunal said in a statement.
The July 1995 indictment, issued against two Serbs, charged the alleged camp commander Goran Jelisic with genocide and another man, Ranko Cesic, with crimes aganst humanity.
The exhumation is intended to provide corroborative evidence to support the charges, which relate to events in 1992.
The international stabilisation force in Bosnia (SFOR) will assist the U.N. investigators by providing a safe environment in which they can work, the tribunal said.
